clue.text: See 11
Leave control of local authority work to solicitor

parts.note: OP is the usual short form of opus, a musical work
a tout is someone who solicits custom, for tickets or trade

explanation.surface: A council hands its legal business over to an outside lawyer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Solicitor' reads as a British lawyer, but here it is a tout, someone touting for business.
explanation.definitionFit: In 1990s Britain schools could opt out, withdrawing from council management to be funded directly.

clue.text: Actress making Bogart rage, uncontrollably

indicators.note: uncontrollably says the letters of the two words run wild into a new order

explanation.surface: A film star drives her co-star Humphrey Bogart into a fury.
explanation.definitionFit: The Swedish star of Ninotchka and Queen Christina is a famous screen actress.

clue.text: See 8
LP I clued poorly, that's very clear

indicators.note: poorly says the letters are badly arranged and must be put right

explanation.surface: A setter admits a long-playing record was badly clued yet insists the clue is obvious.
explanation.definitionFit: Pellucid is a literary synonym for transparent, lucid, easily understood.

clue.text: Share index of paper following return of wintertime in New York

parts.note: F (as in ff.) is the standard abbreviation for following

indicators.note: return of asks for the time zone's letters read backwards

parts.note: New York keeps Eastern Standard Time, EST, in winter

explanation.surface: A paper's stock index after the clocks go back in New York.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition includes 'of paper': the FTSE 100 is run with, and named after, the Financial Times.
explanation.definitionFit: The FTSE 100 is the London stock market's headline index of leading company shares.

clue.text: Peacemakers get pair to separate

parts.note: the United Nations, UN, sends peacekeeping forces
a couple is a pair

explanation.surface: International mediators bring a quarrelling twosome round to splitting up.
explanation.definitionFit: To uncouple is to detach or disconnect, as railway wagons are parted.

clue.text: Sexually attractive man must put in order with Findus — mostly 25, initially

indicators.note: put in order says these letters need rearranging
mostly says the brand name loses its last letter
initially takes just the opening letter of the cross-referenced answer

parts.note: 25 points to the answer at 25 down, the first word of which is a sea creature

explanation.surface: A man must tidy the freezer with Findus, the frozen food brand, mostly fish fingers.
explanation.walkthrough: Findus is a frozen-food brand; 'mostly' drops its S. 25 refers to 25 down, whose first letter F joins MUST and FINDU in the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for a hunky, sexy man: a combination of two terms for a desirable male.

clue.text: Fit in drink with a Parisian after work …

indicators.note: after says the drink and the French word come following the work

parts.note: OP is opus, a work
port is a fortified wine
une is French for a, as a Parisian would say it

explanation.surface: Someone fits in a drink with a French woman once the working day is done.
explanation.definitionFit: Opportune means well timed or suitable, so fit or apt for the occasion.

clue.text: … going back and forth, sharing new belief

parts.note: the ellipsis ties this clue to its own number, ten, which is read as the letters of the word

indicators.note: sharing says the two runs share a letter where they meet, so one copy is lost
going back and forth says the number word is read forwards and then backwards

parts.note: the same number word used again, this time running backwards

explanation.surface: Swinging back and forth on a shared new creed.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis points to the clue number: TEN forwards then NET backwards, the two sharing the N of 'new', give a word reading the same both ways.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenet is a principle or doctrine held as true, so a belief.

clue.text: Botox look worked up to by nasty old woman

parts.note: trout is British slang for an unpleasant old woman, usually 'old trout'

indicators.note: worked says the two small words are worked into a new shape

explanation.surface: A cosmetic face built up to by a disagreeable older woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Worked' looks like a past tense describing the look; it is the anagram signal for 'up to'. 'By' simply joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is tabloid slang for the swollen, pursed lips produced by cosmetic filler injections.

clue.text: Does half of half-cooked pork pie …

indicators.note: cooked says the letters are cooked up into a new arrangement
half- takes only the first half of the little word before it

explanation.surface: A half-baked pork pie loses half of itself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half-cooked' does two jobs: 'half' keeps only the O of 'of', and 'cooked' signals the anagram. 'Pork pie' is British rhyming slang (porky) for a lie.
explanation.definitionFit: In rhyming slang a pork pie, or porky, is a lie, an untrue statement.

clue.text: … turn finally on eating? It'll help to get antibodies

indicators.note: turn says the letters are turned round into a new order
finally takes the last letter of the word on

explanation.surface: Continuing the pork pie story: eating it at last brings on an illness.
explanation.definitionFit: A foreign substance in the body stimulates the immune system to produce antibodies against it.

clue.text: A new setter? One's in heaven, with 25 and 28 to follow

definitions.text: One's in heaven, with 25 and 28 to follow

parts.note: gel sets hair in place, so it is a setter

explanation.surface: A new crossword setter, now departed, is in heaven.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Setter' suggests a crossword compiler; it is hair gel. Followed by the words at 25 and 28 (fish, cakes) the answer gives angelfish and angel cakes.
explanation.definitionFit: Heavenly beings are angels, and the word also prefixes a fish and a cake.

clue.text: Sexually attractive women in Private Eye, twirling skirts round bottom

indicators.note: skirts round says the reversed word wraps both sides of the bottom
twirling turns the detective word round

parts.note: a private eye is a detective, a tec
rump is a bottom

explanation.surface: Pin-ups in the satirical magazine Private Eye twirl their skirts.
explanation.walkthrough: Private Eye is a British satirical magazine, but here it is just a detective; 'twirling' turns that word to CET.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang, now dated and sexist, for women regarded as sexually desirable.

clue.text: Needing no encouragement, concert pianist on vacation gets into playing nude

indicators.note: gets into says the concert and pianist letters go inside
playing says the letters of nude are played about with

parts.note: a prom is a promenade concert, as at the BBC Proms

indicators.note: on vacation empties the word pianist, leaving only its outer letters

explanation.surface: A concert pianist eagerly plays in the nude without being asked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Playing' looks musical but scrambles NUDE to UNDE, into which PROM and PT (pianist emptied) go.
explanation.definitionFit: Unprompted means spontaneous, done without any urging from others.

clue.text: Plants are reportedly in flower

indicators.note: in puts the letter inside the river

parts.note: a flower in crosswords is a river, something that flows; the Tees is a river in north-east England

indicators.note: reportedly says the word is heard, giving the letter it sounds like

parts.note: are is said just like the letter R

explanation.surface: Plants are said to be in bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' reads as a bloom, but it is a river (it flows): the Tees, a river in north-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: Trees are woody perennial plants, the largest members of the plant kingdom.

clue.text: Comparatively bright German philosopher

parts.note: A. J. Ayer was a British logical positivist philosopher

explanation.surface: A clever German thinker.
explanation.definitionFit: Gay in its older sense means cheerful or brightly coloured; the comparative is more so.

clue.text: Goes on about a quiet maiden's headgear

indicators.note: about says the chatter goes round the other pieces

parts.note: yaks means talks on and on
sh is a call for quiet
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: Someone rabbits on about a shy girl's headscarf.
explanation.definitionFit: A veil worn by some Muslim women in public, covering the face below the eyes.

clue.text: Payment method — coin pouch

parts.note: COD stands for cash on delivery
a piece is a coin, as in a fifty-pence piece

explanation.surface: A list of ways to pay: cash in a purse.
explanation.definitionFit: A codpiece was a pouch on the front of men's breeches in Tudor fashion.

clue.text: Line in sweaters sailors embrace passionately

parts.note: a ship's crew are sailors
to neck is to kiss and cuddle

explanation.surface: Sailors in jumpers cuddling on deck.
explanation.definitionFit: A style of knitwear with a round, close-fitting collar is one range or line of jumpers.

clue.text: See 19
12 about model backing Nimble

indicators.note: about says the untruth goes around the model

parts.note: 12 across is a falsehood, another word for which is lie

indicators.note: backing reads the model's name backwards

parts.note: Kate Moss is a famous model

explanation.surface: A falsehood about a model's support for a nimble figure.
explanation.definitionFit: Lissome means lithe, supple and graceful, so agile.

clue.text: Some bits pong, especially bums

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Bits of someone smell, especially their backsides.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bums' is the verb: to bum is to scrounge.
explanation.definitionFit: To sponge is to cadge or freeload off others, as one who bums cigarettes.

clue.text: Pinkish political leader taking day off

indicators.note: taking ... off says the letter is removed

parts.note: Alex Salmond was the leader of the Scottish National Party and First Minister of Scotland

explanation.surface: A left-leaning politician takes a day off.
explanation.walkthrough: Alex Salmond was Scotland's First Minister when this appeared; drop the D.
explanation.definitionFit: The colour of the fish's flesh, an orange-pink shade, is a colour adjective.

clue.text: Chap with wandering hands? Mildred's husband, in short

indicators.note: in short cuts the first name down to its initial

parts.note: George Roper was Mildred's husband in the 1970s British sitcom George and Mildred
his surname is the second half of the name

explanation.surface: A sitcom husband suspected of straying hands.
explanation.walkthrough: George and Mildred was a 1970s British sitcom; its husband G. Roper, written with an initial, spells the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who fondles others without consent; the question mark flags a jokey definition.

clue.text: Round of 4 provided in influentially important case

indicators.note: in puts the condition inside the other word

parts.note: a seminal case is one of great influence on what follows
if means provided, on condition that

explanation.surface: A legal ruling hinges on an important precedent.
explanation.definitionFit: The penultimate stage of a knockout competition, contested by the last four.

clue.text: Blow taking out 22 down's eye

indicators.note: taking out says the following word is removed

parts.note: 22 down is salmon, and the sockeye is a kind of salmon
taken as written

explanation.surface: A punch knocks out a fish's eye.
explanation.definitionFit: A sock is a hard punch or blow, in informal usage.

clue.text: Having ordered these, gives chef a 27?

definitions.text: Having ordered these, gives chef a 27?

indicators.note: ordered does double duty: a diner orders the dish, and the words are put in a new order

parts.note: 27 down is a caress, a kiss

explanation.surface: A diner so pleased with the dish that they kiss the chef.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of CHEF A KISS gives the dish; 'ordered' serves both as the restaurant order and the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Patties of flaked fish mixed with potato are a dish one could order from a chef.

clue.text: Noisily put down drink

definitions.meaning: to set something down heavily with a thud

explanation.surface: Someone bangs down a glass.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to set down with a thump and cheap, low-quality wine.

clue.text: Caress runners after cycling

indicators.note: cycling moves a letter round from one end of the word to the other

parts.note: skis are runners on snow

explanation.surface: A stroke for athletes after a bike ride.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runners' suggests athletes but is skis; moving the first S to the end gives KISS.
explanation.definitionFit: A kiss is a gentle touch with the lips, an affectionate caress.

clue.text: See 25
Intimacy of head on bosom

indicators.note: on, in an across clue, puts the headland after the other piece

parts.note: a bosom friend is a close friend
a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness or Sheerness

explanation.surface: A tender moment with a head resting on a chest.
explanation.definitionFit: Closeness and intimacy are near-synonyms for a deep personal bond.
